concept.name: Bid volume
concept.definition: The total traded volume classified as having occurred at the bid price — trades initiated by aggressive sellers whose market or marketable sell orders matched resting buy limit orders. It is the sell-initiated component of bid/ask order-flow analysis.
concept.intuition: Bid volume measures how much selling was aggressive enough to cross the spread and hit the prices buyers had posted.
concept.mechanics: Each trade is classified as a bid trade when the exchange feed flags it as executed at the bid, or heuristically when its price is at or below the prevailing bid (or on a downtick when trade and quote data are unsynchronized); classified volumes are then summed per price level, bar, or session.
concept.failure_modes: Classification depends on data quality: feeds without exchange-provided trade-side flags must infer the side from ticks, which misclassifies trades when quote and trade streams are out of sync.
concept.misconceptions: Bid volume is not net selling that removes ownership — every bid-side trade still has a buyer; it records which side was the aggressor, not a change in net positions.
concept.example: In a one-minute bar, 800 contracts trade at the bid and 300 at the ask; bid volume of 800 shows sellers were the more aggressive side that minute.
